newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-GARRIDO OPENS UP THREE-SHOT LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GARRIDO OPENS UP THREE-SHOT LEAD.

text.p: Spain's Ignacio Garrido opened up an early three-shot lead in the German Open on Friday while Briton Mark James moved into second place, partly due to his first tournament hole-in-one in a 20-year career.
The week after winning the Spanish PGA title in Madrid, a none European Tour event, Garrido's second round four-under-par 67 took him to 10-under-par, three ahead of James who also carded 67.
Garrido rolled home a 30ft putt on the last for birdie soon after James had produced his ace at the penultimate hole.
The 25-year-old Spaniard is seeking to go one better than three second places he has had on Tour since joining in 1994. His third runner-up spot came in March's Portuguese Open.
A tip given to him by his uncle German Garrido, a former European Tour pro as was the leader's father Antonio, before the final round of last week's victory in Madrid has turned his game, he said.

"My uncle noticed I was using my hands too much which meant I kept hooking and pulling when I am a natural fader of the ball," said Garrido. "I felt much happier after adjusting my swing and that helped me shoot a 68 in the wind in Madrid and I won by three.

The young Spaniard, who qualified for the European Tour in 1994 after winning the 1993 Spanish PGA for the first time, could make it only the second time a son has followed his father in qualifying for the Ryder Cup team. Englishmen Percy and Peter Alliss were the other pair.

Father Antonio was compatriot Severiano Ballesteros's first partner when the present Ryder Cup captain made his Cup debut in 1979. However, Ignacio Garrido, who currently lies 33rd in the Cup table, is keeping his feet on the ground, even though last year he had firmly forecast he would be in Ballesteros's Valderrama squad.
"Maybe I should not have said that, maybe I was just joking," he said. "I don't want to even think about it because it puts on so much pressure.

"I have a lot of years to come but perhaps I'm not consistent enough, not prepared well enough for this one. My goal first is to win on Tour and if I win twice and get into the top-10 automatic places then I will know I was prepared. Some year though it will be son following father in the Ryder Cup again."

James charged into second place by holing out with a five-iron on the 194-yard eighth, his 17th hole. "It's amazing that this is my first hole in one in a tournament but that perhaps shows how bad my iron play has been over the years," joked the 43-year-old Englishman.

James lies 21st in the Ryder Cup table but dismissed suggestions of an eighth team place if he wins this week. "I'd need to win this week and earn another 100,000 points and that may be too much," he said.
